stories.title: Deloitte spins up a new AI company, Edisyl
stories.pre: Deloitte spins up a new AI company,
stories.summary: Deloitte's venture arm, D71 Ventures, bought the AI business of Flipside Crypto and relaunched it as Edisyl, a standalone enterprise AI company.
why: The Big Four are moving from advising on AI to owning AI products, which earn money outside billable hours.
Deloitte used its venture arm to buy a ready-made team and technology instead of building from scratch.
Watch how audit-independence rules apply when an audit firm also owns AI companies it could sell to clients.
stories.cs: Rival firms' boards will ask whether they should buy AI companies too, and acquired AI businesses need integration and go-to-market help.
stories.take: The Big Four no longer just advise on AI. They're buying and launching AI companies, and more will follow.
paras: Deloitte has bought its way into another AI business. Its venture arm, D71 Ventures, has acquired the AI business of Flipside Crypto and relaunched it as Edisyl, a new standalone enterprise AI company, Consultancy.org reported on November 13.

Flipside is a Boston-based firm best known for blockchain data and analytics tools for crypto organisations. According to CB Insights, it raised about $65.7 million over seven funding rounds and was valued at $350 million in April 2022.

The deal fits a broader push at Deloitte. Its US arm launched Zora AI, a suite of AI agents, and the firm then set up a Global Agentic Network to build agents for clients. Bloomberg Law reported in September that Deloitte is almost halfway through a five-year commitment to spend $3 billion on AI.
unknowns: What Deloitte paid. No price has been reported.
How many Flipside staff are moving to Edisyl.
What Edisyl will sell, and whether Deloitte audit clients will be allowed to buy it.

stories.title: Mercor raises $750M to have human experts test AI agents
stories.summary: Mercor, which started as an AI hiring platform and now connects professionals with companies training AI, raised $750M to expand evaluation of agents that do professional work.
stories.cs: HR and L&D leaders will need plans for junior roles as experts train the agents that do the work.

stories.title: BCG: companies now spend 3.3% of revenue on AI, almost double late 2025
stories.summary: BCG estimates AI investment has climbed to 3.3% of revenue from 1.7% in late 2025, but payoffs stay patchy because human sign-offs remain after AI does the task.
stories.cs: Every CFO funding AI will ask where the payoff is: workflow redesign and ROI-tracking work.

stories.title: Anthropic ships Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2
stories.summary: New models aimed at complex engineering, agent coordination and technical work. Accenture's Cyber.AI security service already runs on Claude.
stories.cs: Clients will re-run build-vs-buy decisions on agents: expect vendor-selection work.

stories.title: McKinsey's State of AI: agent use climbs as companies build rather than buy
stories.summary: A read of McKinsey's 2026 survey: agentic AI use is rising, led by large enterprises, and more companies are building their own software.
stories.cs: Build-over-buy means more custom engineering projects, not just software licences.

bigMoves.title: Nvidia's board opens a probe into CEO Jensen Huang
bigMoves.body: Independent directors launched an investigation into reports that Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort. The board says it has no reason to believe company information was compromised, and the allegations have not been established.
bigMoves.cs: A live case of key-person risk at a $4.5 trillion company. Boards and their advisers will be stress-testing succession plans.
bigMoves.take: Whatever the probe finds, every board just got a reminder to have a real succession plan.

bigMoves.title: Anthropic files for what could be the largest IPO ever
bigMoves.cs: Mega-IPOs mean months of readiness work: governance, controls and investor storytelling.

bigMoves.title: Marvell's Lumentum deal dwarfs every other AI acquisition this month
bigMoves.cs: Chip supply chains are consolidating. Integration at this scale is huge advisory work.

bigMoves.title: Ottawa agrees to invest up to $1.14B in Cohere
bigMoves.cs: Sovereign AI is now industrial policy. Expect public-sector AI strategy work in Canada.

bigMoves.cs: Defence tech is consolidating fast, a growing niche for strategy and deal teams.

howItWorks.title: How Chipotle runs a restaurant
howItWorks.body: Company-owned stores, a short menu and an assembly line built for speed. The economics come down to how many orders each store can push through at the lunch peak.
howItWorks.ai: digital ordering lanes, kitchen automation, staffing forecasts.
howItWorks.caseq: Chipotle wants to raise throughput 10% without adding staff. What are your levers?

howItWorks.title: How Amazon really works
howItWorks.body: The store is the part you see, but the profit mostly comes from AWS and advertising. Retail is a volume and logistics machine that feeds both.
howItWorks.ai: warehouse robotics, demand forecasting, and selling AI to everyone else through AWS.
howItWorks.caseq: Should Amazon spin off AWS? Build the argument for each side.

howItWorks.title: How trucking actually makes money
howItWorks.body: Freight is paid by the mile, but trucks often drive back empty. A huge, fragmented market of small carriers, brokers in the middle, and constant driver turnover.
howItWorks.ai: load matching, route and fuel optimisation, automated brokerage.
howItWorks.caseq: A mid-sized carrier's margins fell two years in a row. Where do you look first?
